changelog.summary: ADR 0037 - seven more rules implemented in the referral engine (evaluate_<rule>() functions, wired into evaluate_application_referrals(); the orchestrator now composes twelve rules, one decision_log row each): VV-03, VV-04, DH-03, DH-04, AL-02, CP-01, PC-01. All read only fields already present in the application schema. Notes: VV-03 implements the currency/staleness limb only (missing/stale appraisal when agreed value is requested); the '115% of appraised value' limb is deferred because there is no requested agreed-value AMOUNT field in the schema (only the boolean agreed_value_requested and current_appraised_value). VV-03 reads the reappraisal interval live from state_rating_table_versions.agreed_value_rules.reappraisal_interval_years for the garaging state, falling back to a 3-year national default when the state is not onboarded or the value is null/'TBD'. CP-01's heuristic is concrete: pleasure/commute annual_mileage >= 20000, OR a commercial-driving occupation keyword with a single pleasure vehicle. PC-01 fires on a garaging-state != mailing-state mismatch; its territory_rating_basis state_override_hook is descriptive metadata, not rule logic. DH-04 gates only submitted (not draft) applications - submit_application was reordered (ADR 0031 -> 0037) to set status before evaluating so first submissions are checked. Still unimplemented (need external data sources): VV-01, VV-02, DH-02, PC-02 (sanctions/OFAC), PC-04.

ADR 0036 - two independent rule-logic changes from different sources. (1) DH-01 (source: insurance-domain colleague's email, 'same five year look to keep it simple'): reckless-driving convictions now fire DH-01 on the same 5-year look-back and the same MANUAL_REVIEW_SENIOR severity as DUI, with a type-aware reason_code (DH01_DUI_WITHIN_LOOKBACK / DH01_RECKLESS_WITHIN_LOOKBACK, DUI precedence when both present, still one decision_log row per rule). (2) PC-03 (source: founder directive, reframed around the all-50-states v1 rollout): out-of-territory routes to AUTO_PROCEED_WITH_FLAG instead of MANUAL_REVIEW_REQUIRED - it still fires and still logs its reason_code (rule 4), but no longer blocks on a human for a not-yet-onboarded state; this does not make such a state quotable. Resolves the open_items PC-03 entry (soft-warn).

source_fields updated to point at the formal enrichment_computed section added to the application schema in v1.1, replacing the ad hoc 'external: ...' placeholders used in v1.0. No rule logic changed - only the field paths these rules read from.

purpose: Defines every condition that must route an application away from straight-through auto-quote, and what happens when it does. This is the pipeline's hard-stop layer - the place where 'the model isn't sure' or 'the model is sure but the answer requires a human/compliance check' gets encoded as executable logic rather than left to discretion under deadline pressure.
how_this_is_used: 1. Every rule below is evaluated against the incoming application (post data-enrichment: MVR, VIN decode, title history, prior-carrier loss run) BEFORE the rating engine runs, the same way the Energy manual gates pricing on aggregate/referral checks before the worksheet is touched.
2. A rule firing does not necessarily mean decline - see action_taxonomy. Most rules route to a human underwriter or an automated information request, not an auto-decline.

3. Rules with a state_override_hook must be checked against that state's active state_rating_table record (referral_thresholds_state_specific or prohibited_variables) - a state can tighten, loosen, or add disclosure requirements around a nationally-defined trigger.

4. Every rule that fires must write a reason_code to the application's decision log, unredacted, even if the ultimate outcome is 'proceed.' This is what makes an adverse-action explanation or a market conduct exam answerable later - see the NY DFS Circular Letter 2024-7 requirement in the state registry's ai_governance section, which this matrix is designed to satisfy by default.
5. Declinations require the reason_code to be captured at the point of decision, not reconstructed later - directly mirroring the Energy manual's Chapter 3 clearance discipline.

action_taxonomy.AUTO_PROCEED: No referral. Rating engine runs normally.
action_taxonomy.AUTO_PROCEED_WITH_FLAG: Rating engine runs, but the flag and its basis are attached to the file for later review (e.g. periodic audit sampling) - not blocking.
action_taxonomy.INFORMATION_REQUEST: Pipeline halts and generates a specific, itemized request back to the applicant/broker. Not a referral to a human underwriter yet - a data completeness gate.
action_taxonomy.MANUAL_REVIEW_REQUIRED: Routed to a human underwriter before any quote is issued. The pipeline may still compute a provisional/indicative price for the underwriter's use, but it cannot be released to the applicant unsupervised.
action_taxonomy.MANUAL_REVIEW_SENIOR: Same as above, but requires review by a senior underwriter or a second sign-off (peer review), reserved for the highest-severity triggers.
action_taxonomy.DECLINE_RECOMMENDED: Pipeline recommends decline with the reason_code pre-filled, but a human confirms - full auto-decline is not used anywhere in this matrix. See design_note below.
action_taxonomy.HARD_DECLINE_COMPLIANCE: Reserved for sanctions/legal hits only. No human discretion - if this fires, the application cannot proceed regardless of any other factor.

design_note: No category below auto-declines purely on a model decision except HARD_DECLINE_COMPLIANCE (sanctions). This is a deliberate choice, not an oversight: an AI-driven decline with no human in the loop is exactly the fact pattern that draws NAIC Model Bulletin and state DFS/DOI scrutiny (see prior registry's ai_governance notes). DECLINE_RECOMMENDED keeps a human as the accountable decision-maker while still giving them a fully-reasoned pipeline output to confirm or override.

vehicle_and_valuation.trigger: VIN decode result does not match applicant-declared make/model/trim/year
vehicle_and_valuation.illustrative_threshold: Any mismatch in make, model, or model year; trim-level mismatches route lower-severity unless they change vehicle_category (e.g. base trim vs. high-performance variant)
vehicle_and_valuation.rationale: Could be a data-entry error or an attempt to insure a higher-value vehicle under a cheaper vehicle's declared description. Pipeline cannot distinguish intent, so it cannot resolve this itself.
vehicle_and_valuation.test_case_reference: Edge case: VIN-to-declared-vehicle mismatch (APP-0009, Corvette Stingray declared / Z06 decoded)

vehicle_and_valuation.trigger: Title history check returns salvage, rebuilt, or flood designation not disclosed anywhere in the application
vehicle_and_valuation.rationale: Undisclosed title issues on a high-value vehicle materially change both the correct agreed value and the accuracy of the risk being priced. Self-reported condition alone is not a sufficient control - this is exactly why the pipeline runs an independent title-history check rather than relying on the form.

vehicle_and_valuation.trigger: Agreed value requested exceeds a multiple of the most recent independent appraisal, or appraisal is missing/stale
vehicle_and_valuation.illustrative_threshold: Agreed value > 115% of appraised value, or appraisal_date older than reappraisal_interval_years from the applicable state rating table
vehicle_and_valuation.rationale: Agreed value is only meaningful with a current, credible valuation basis. This is a completeness/currency gate, not a risk judgment - resolve it before it reaches an underwriter.
vehicle_and_valuation.implementation: ADR 0037: implemented as evaluate_vv03() - the missing/stale-appraisal limb only (fires INFORMATION_REQUEST when a vehicle requests agreed value and its appraisal_date is null or older than the reappraisal interval). The '115% of appraised value' limb is NOT implemented: no requested agreed-value amount field exists. Interval read live from agreed_value_rules.reappraisal_interval_years, 3-year national default fallback.

vehicle_and_valuation.trigger: Vehicle has performance/security modifications materially affecting value or risk profile that are not reflected in the declared value or vehicle_category
vehicle_and_valuation.illustrative_threshold: Any modification field populated where vehicle_category is still 'production_luxury' rather than 'modified_performance'
vehicle_and_valuation.rationale: Modifications change both theft/collision severity and the correct agreed value basis - mirrors the moderate-risk sample profile already in your test set.
vehicle_and_valuation.test_case_reference: Sample application: moderate-risk young driver with modified performance vehicle
vehicle_and_valuation.implementation: ADR 0037: implemented as evaluate_vv04() - fires when a vehicle has a non-blank modifications value but vehicle_category is still production_luxury.

driver_and_household.trigger: DUI or reckless-driving conviction within the applicable look-back period
driver_and_household.illustrative_threshold: Any DUI OR reckless-driving conviction within a 5-year look-back (national default). Reckless driving was folded into the same 5-year look-back and the same MANUAL_REVIEW_SENIOR severity as DUI in ADR 0036 (v1.2) - no separate threshold ('same five year look to keep it simple'). Convictions only.
driver_and_household.rationale: DUI is treated as a hard referral in every HNW carrier program reviewed for this build, regardless of how clean the rest of the profile is (see the sample application where an otherwise strong applicant with a DUI required SR-22/FR-44 and non-standard routing). Reckless-driving convictions are treated identically as of ADR 0036 on the same rationale.
driver_and_household.test_case_reference: Edge case: DUI history requiring hard referral routing (APP-0007)
driver_and_household.reason_code: DH01_DUI_WITHIN_LOOKBACK for a DUI conviction, DH01_RECKLESS_WITHIN_LOOKBACK for a reckless-driving conviction; DUI takes precedence in the code when both are present within the window, and the matched type(s) are recorded in the decision-log notes (one decision_log row per rule regardless)

driver_and_household.trigger: Household/garaging-address data (e.g. shared last name at same address, prior-carrier household driver list, credit household match) indicates a licensed driver at the address who is not declared on the application
driver_and_household.illustrative_threshold: Any positive match not reconciled by the applicant
driver_and_household.rationale: An undisclosed household driver is a coverage gap and a rating-accuracy problem at once - the risk being priced isn't the risk that actually exists at that address.

driver_and_household.trigger: Any listed driver (applicant or additional) has a suspended or revoked license status
driver_and_household.illustrative_threshold: license_status = suspended or revoked, for applicant or any additional_drivers entry
driver_and_household.rationale: Mirrors the high-risk sample profile in your existing test set (suspended additional driver + poor claims history) - this combination has historically been one of the clearest hard-stop patterns in HNW auto underwriting.
driver_and_household.test_case_reference: Sample application: high-risk applicant with poor claims history and suspended additional driver
driver_and_household.implementation: ADR 0037: implemented as evaluate_dh03() - fires MANUAL_REVIEW_SENIOR when applicant or any additional driver has license_status suspended or revoked (expired does not count).

driver_and_household.trigger: Required applicant or driver fields are null/missing at a rate that prevents any risk computation
driver_and_household.illustrative_threshold: Any of: date_of_birth, license_status, years_licensed, garaging_address, or vin is null on a submitted (not draft) application
driver_and_household.rationale: The pipeline must not default-fill or silently proceed on missing risk-critical fields - it must explicitly ask, not guess. This is the completeness gate your incomplete-application edge case was specifically built to exercise.
driver_and_household.test_case_reference: Edge case: incomplete application with widespread null fields (APP-0008)
driver_and_household.implementation: ADR 0037: implemented as evaluate_dh04() - fires INFORMATION_REQUEST on a SUBMITTED (not draft) application missing applicant date_of_birth/license_status/years_licensed or any vehicle's vin/garaging_street. submit_application sets status before evaluating so first submissions are gated.

account_and_loss_history.trigger: 5-year claims history shows a loss ratio or claim frequency above the carrier's referral trigger
account_and_loss_history.illustrative_threshold: 2+ at-fault claims in 5 years, or any single claim exceeding a defined severity threshold
account_and_loss_history.rationale: Direct analogue to the Energy manual's 'five-year loss ratio above binder trigger' referral - the threshold itself is a business decision to be set with underwriting leadership, not inferred by the pipeline.
account_and_loss_history.test_case_reference: Sample application: high-risk applicant with poor claims history

account_and_loss_history.trigger: Prior carrier non-renewal or cancellation history disclosed or discovered
account_and_loss_history.rationale: Why a carrier chose not to renew is exactly the kind of context a model shouldn't resolve unilaterally - the reason matters more than the fact.
account_and_loss_history.implementation: ADR 0037: implemented as evaluate_al02() - fires when prior_insurance.any_nonrenewal_or_cancellation_history is true; a missing prior_insurance row is not a trigger.

coverage_and_pricing.trigger: Vehicle's stated primary_use is pleasure/commute but usage pattern data (annual_mileage, occupation, garaging pattern) suggests undisclosed business use (ride-share, livery, business delivery)
coverage_and_pricing.illustrative_threshold: annual_mileage inconsistent with declared use pattern, or occupation field suggests a business-use vehicle (e.g. real estate agent + primary_use = pleasure on the only vehicle on the policy)
coverage_and_pricing.rationale: Business-use misrepresentation changes the entire coverage form that should apply, not just the price - a personal auto policy may not respond to a business-use loss at all.
coverage_and_pricing.implementation: ADR 0037: implemented as evaluate_cp01() - fires MANUAL_REVIEW_REQUIRED on EITHER a pleasure/commute vehicle with annual_mileage >= 20000, OR a commercial-driving occupation keyword (rideshare/uber/lyft/livery/taxi/chauffeur/courier/delivery/real estate/realtor) with a single pleasure vehicle. Thresholds/keywords are tunable knobs.

coverage_and_pricing.trigger: Requested coverage exceeds delegated/program authority (line size, umbrella limit, or aggregate TIV across all vehicles on the application)
coverage_and_pricing.illustrative_threshold: Combined agreed value across vehicles on one application above the program's per-risk authority cap
coverage_and_pricing.rationale: Direct analogue to the Energy manual's capacity/aggregate referral category - anything above delegated authority goes up, full stop, regardless of how clean the rest of the risk looks.
coverage_and_pricing.test_case_reference: Sample application: exotic edge case with agreed-value complexity

coverage_and_pricing.trigger: A rating credit is being applied beyond the state's approved credit/debit band
coverage_and_pricing.illustrative_threshold: Per the active state_rating_table record's approved_rating_variables band restrictions
source_fields: computed at rating time, not a form field
coverage_and_pricing.rationale: This is a compliance stop, not a risk stop - it should never fire if the rating engine is correctly bounded by the state registry, but it exists as a second independent check so a registry defect doesn't silently produce a non-compliant quote.

process_and_conduct.trigger: Garaging address does not match the applicant's stated mailing/residential address, or shows a pattern consistent with rate evasion (e.g. garaging listed in a lower-rated territory than where the applicant plausibly lives/works)
process_and_conduct.illustrative_threshold: Garaging state/territory differs from mailing state/territory without a documented reason (e.g. seasonal residence, storage facility)
process_and_conduct.rationale: Territory is one of the most heavily-weighted rating variables in every state reviewed - an unexplained mismatch is the single highest-value rate-evasion signal available before a human even looks at the file.
process_and_conduct.test_case_reference: Edge case: garaging address mismatch/rate evasion
process_and_conduct.implementation: ADR 0037: implemented as evaluate_pc01() - fires when applications.garaging_state differs from applicants.mailing_state (null mailing_state -> not fired). territory_rating_basis is descriptive metadata, not a gate. The 'documented reason' exception is not yet representable; the human reviewer weighs it.

process_and_conduct.trigger: Sanctions/OFAC screen returns a positive hit on the applicant or any named driver
process_and_conduct.rationale: The only fully automated stop in this matrix - no underwriting judgment applies to a sanctions hit.

process_and_conduct.trigger: Application is out-of-territory for the program (garaging state not currently licensed/active for this product)
process_and_conduct.illustrative_threshold: Garaging state has no active state_rating_table record
process_and_conduct.rationale: Not a risk judgment - a licensing fact. Routed to AUTO_PROCEED_WITH_FLAG as of ADR 0036 (v1.2), changed from MANUAL_REVIEW_REQUIRED: the platform's v1 scope is all 50 US states and onboarding is a rollout in progress, so 'no active state_rating_table record' is the expected interim state for any state not yet onboarded, not a licensing red flag. The rule still fires and still writes its reason_code to the decision log (rule 4) - the flag is attached to the file for later review, it just no longer routes to a human before proceeding. NOTE: this does NOT make an un-onboarded state quotable - create_quote() still requires a real rating record + territory factor and fails with TERRITORY_FACTOR_NOT_CONFIGURED for any state that has not gone through onboard_state() (ADR 0035). The 50-state rollout is tracked as a separate initiative.
process_and_conduct.state_override_hook: existence of an active record for the state in question

process_and_conduct.trigger: Broker/agent placing the business is not yet verified (licensing, appointment status) at time of submission
process_and_conduct.illustrative_threshold: No verified producer record on file
process_and_conduct.rationale: Direct analogue to the Energy manual's 'new producer pre-TOBA' referral trigger.

open_items_for_underwriting_leadership: Set actual numeric thresholds for AL-01 (loss ratio/claim frequency trigger) and CP-02 (aggregate TIV authority cap) - these were left illustrative because they're business risk-appetite decisions, not something derivable from regulation.

Confirm whether DH-01's national 5-year DUI look-back default is correct, or whether it should simply require a per-state value with no fallback (safer, but blocks quoting in any state not yet in the registry).

RESOLVED (ADR 0036, v1.2): PC-03 (out-of-territory) is soft-warn, not hard-block. It now routes to AUTO_PROCEED_WITH_FLAG rather than MANUAL_REVIEW_REQUIRED - the platform's v1 scope is all 50 US states with onboarding in progress, so a missing state_rating_table record is the expected interim state during rollout rather than 'not licensed.' The rule still fires and still logs its reason_code. This does not make an un-onboarded state quotable: create_quote() still fails with TERRITORY_FACTOR_NOT_CONFIGURED until the state goes through onboard_state().
